requirements: The core contributions of the paper 'Hybrid JIT-CUDA Graph Optimization for Low-Latency Large Language Model Inference' have been reproduced.

sub_tasks.requirements: Environment, model, and dependency prerequisites are correctly set up.
Code has been implemented using PyTorch 2.3 as the deep learning framework.

verification.spec: Import torch and assert torch.__version__.startswith('2.3').

sub_tasks.requirements: Code has been implemented using CUDA 12.4 toolkit for GPU execution.

verification.spec: Check torch.version.cuda equals '12.4' and/or run nvcc --version and parse the release string to confirm CUDA 12.4 toolkit is installed.

sub_tasks.requirements: Experiments are run on an NVIDIA H100 GPU (94 GB HBM3).

verification.spec: Run nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total --format=csv and assert the GPU name contains 'H100' and reported total memory is approximately 94 GB (>=90000 MiB).

sub_tasks.requirements: The LLaMA-2 7B model has been acquired and loaded for inference.

verification.spec: Load LLaMA-2 7B via transformers AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained('meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf'), assert config.hidden_size==4096, config.num_hidden_layers==32, and a single forward pass on a dummy input_ids tensor returns logits of shape (1, seq, 32000).

sub_tasks.requirements: TensorRT-LLM 1.0 has been installed and configured for baseline comparison.

verification.spec: Import tensorrt_llm and assert tensorrt_llm.__version__.startswith('1.0'); verify a LLaMA engine can be built or loaded for inference.

sub_tasks.requirements: HuggingFace Transformers library is installed and capable of running LLaMA-2 7B inference for baseline comparison.

verification.spec: Import transformers, load LlamaForCausalLM with the LLaMA-2 7B weights, run model.generate on a short prompt and assert generated token IDs of expected shape are returned without errors.

sub_tasks.requirements: All experiments use FP16 precision via torch.autocast.

verification.spec: Grep the inference code for torch.autocast(..., dtype=torch.float16) usage wrapping the model forward pass, and confirm via runtime hook that tensor dtypes inside the autocast region are float16.

sub_tasks.requirements: All experiments use batch size 1 for latency-sensitive evaluation.

verification.spec: Inspect the benchmark/runtime code and assert that the input_ids batch dimension is hardcoded or configured to 1; instrument the model forward call to assert input.shape[0]==1 across all benchmark iterations.

sub_tasks.requirements: All runs use deterministic seeds to ensure reproducibility.

verification.spec: Inspect the benchmark/runtime source: confirm that explicit deterministic seeds are set for torch, numpy, random, and torch.cuda (e.g., torch.manual_seed, torch.cuda.manual_seed_all, numpy.random.seed) before inference runs. Additionally verify that running the benchmark twice with the same seed produces identical generated token sequences (greedy or seeded-stochastic).

sub_tasks.requirements: Warm-start caching is enabled to ensure measurement stability.

verification.spec: Inspect the benchmark harness: confirm that prior to timed measurements a warm-up phase executes (e.g., several throwaway forward passes / pre-captured short-sequence graphs for lengths 1-50) and that CUDA caching allocator state is primed. Verify measurement loop discards the first N warm-up iterations.

sub_tasks.requirements: The static vs. dynamic operation classification described in Section III-A has been implemented.
Static operations (linear projections, layer normalization, matrix multiplications, attention score computation) are identified and routed to CUDA Graph capture.

verification.spec: Construct an instrumented runtime that wraps each operator with a tag; run one decoding step and verify that linear projections, layer normalization, matrix multiplications, and attention score (qk^T) computations are executed inside a torch.cuda.CUDAGraph capture/replay region, while other ops are not.

sub_tasks.requirements: Dynamic operations (token sampling, KV-cache updates, positional embedding extension) are identified and routed to the JIT execution path.

verification.spec: Instrument the runtime: run a few decoding iterations and verify that token sampling, KV-cache updates, and positional embedding extension execute outside CUDA Graph regions and are dispatched through JIT-compiled (torch.jit / TorchScript) functions, while static segments are inside captured graphs.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Hybrid JIT-CUDA Graph runtime described in Algorithm 1 has been implemented.
Context initialization is implemented: two CUDA streams S_cap (capture) and S_rep (replay) are created.

verification.spec: Inspect the runtime initialization code: verify two distinct torch.cuda.Stream objects are instantiated and named/used as capture stream (S_cap) and replay stream (S_rep). Confirm graph capture operations use S_cap and graph replay uses S_rep.

sub_tasks.requirements: CUDA Graphs for short-sequence lengths in the range [1, 50] are pre-captured during warm-up initialization.

verification.spec: After running the runtime initialization, inspect the rolling graph buffer G and assert that CUDA Graphs keyed by sequence lengths 1..50 are present before the first user decoding step.

sub_tasks.requirements: An IPC channel is established between the Context Generator (Process 1) and Graph Generator (Process 2).

verification.spec: Inspect the runtime: confirm two separate processes (Context Generator and Graph Generator) are spawned (e.g., via multiprocessing) and that an IPC channel (Pipe, Queue, shared memory, or CUDA IPC handles) is established between them. Verify channel handles are constructed during initialization.

sub_tasks.requirements: The Context Generator performs JIT-based preprocessing of token context x_i at each decoding step i.

verification.spec: Invoke a single decoding step of the Context Generator with a sample token id; verify that the preprocessing function is JIT-compiled (e.g., isinstance(fn, torch.jit.ScriptFunction) or torch.jit.ScriptModule) and returns the preprocessed context tensor x_i with expected shape/dtype.

sub_tasks.requirements: Preprocessed token context x_i is sent from Context Generator to Graph Generator via the IPC channel.

verification.spec: Run a single iteration of the decoding loop with the two processes; verify that the preprocessed context tensor x_i produced by Context Generator is transmitted via the IPC channel and received by the Graph Generator (e.g., assert recv tensor equals sent tensor).

sub_tasks.requirements: When a matching CUDA Graph G_l for the current sequence length exists in the rolling buffer G, it is replayed on stream S_rep to compute hidden states h_i.

verification.spec: Pre-populate G with a graph for sequence length L, then call decode at length L. Instrument the runtime to log which path is taken and verify the replay path on stream S_rep is invoked (graph.replay() called) and that hidden states are produced matching a reference forward pass within fp16 tolerance.

sub_tasks.requirements: When no matching CUDA Graph exists, the static segment is executed via JIT and a new graph G_l is asynchronously captured on stream S_cap.

verification.spec: Start with an empty graph buffer G, invoke decode at sequence length L not in G; instrument the runtime to log that (a) the static segment ran via JIT, (b) a new CUDA Graph for length L was captured on a separate capture stream S_cap, and (c) the capture happened asynchronously (capture stream != main stream).

sub_tasks.requirements: Newly captured graphs are inserted into the rolling buffer G with a least-used eviction policy when capacity is exceeded.

verification.spec: Configure the rolling buffer G with a small capacity (e.g., 3); trigger captures for 4 distinct sequence lengths and assert that after insertion the buffer size equals capacity and the least-used graph (lowest replay count or oldest access timestamp) has been evicted.

sub_tasks.requirements: Hidden state h_i is returned to the Context Generator after replay or capture.

verification.spec: Execute one decoding step; verify that after the Graph Generator computes hidden state h_i via either CUDA Graph replay or JIT execution, h_i is returned via IPC to the Context Generator with expected shape (hidden_dim,) and dtype float16.

sub_tasks.requirements: Token t_i is decoded from hidden state h_i via JIT-compiled sampling function f_decode.

verification.spec: Invoke f_decode(h_i) on a fixed hidden-state tensor; verify it is a JIT-compiled function (torch.jit.ScriptFunction/Module) that returns a single token id (integer tensor). With a fixed seed, verify it produces deterministic output.

sub_tasks.requirements: Cleanup phase synchronizes streams and releases inactive graphs from the rolling buffer G.

verification.spec: Inspect cleanup code path: confirm calls to torch.cuda.synchronize() (or per-stream synchronize on S_cap and S_rep) and that inactive CUDA Graphs are removed from the rolling buffer G (e.g., del / buffer.clear()). Trigger cleanup and verify buffer size decreases.

sub_tasks.requirements: The CUDA Graph capture and replay mechanism is implemented correctly.
CUDA Graphs are implemented using the torch.cuda.CUDAGraph API.

verification.spec: Grep the source for `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` instantiation and `graph.capture_begin()/capture_end()` or `with torch.cuda.graph(...)` usage. Confirm graphs are constructed via this API rather than custom CUDA driver wrappers.

sub_tasks.requirements: Capture streams use cudaStreamCaptureModeThreadLocal to enable overlap between replay and capture.

verification.spec: Search source for graph capture invocation and assert it uses torch.cuda.graph(..., capture_error_mode='thread_local') or the underlying cudaStreamBeginCaptureToGraph with cudaStreamCaptureModeThreadLocal flag.

sub_tasks.requirements: Each CUDA Graph encapsulates the GPU execution DAG of matrix multiplications, fused attention kernels, and normalization layers for one fixed sequence length.

verification.spec: Capture a graph for a fixed sequence length and use torch.profiler or nsys to enumerate kernels recorded inside the graph. Verify the kernel list includes (a) matrix multiplication / GEMM kernels (cublas/cutlass), (b) fused attention kernels (FlashAttention), and (c) layer normalization kernels. Verify each captured graph corresponds to one specific sequence length.

sub_tasks.requirements: All static CUDA Graphs share a common activation workspace, enabling reuse of temporary buffers across graphs to reduce VRAM consumption.

verification.spec: Capture two or more CUDA Graphs for different sequence lengths and inspect the activation/intermediate-buffer pointers used by each graph (e.g., via tensor.data_ptr() on the workspace tensor). Verify they share the same underlying allocation (same data_ptr base). Additionally compare total VRAM usage with and without shared workspace; verify shared workspace uses less memory.

sub_tasks.requirements: Background capture threads are used for asynchronous graph generation after initialization.

verification.spec: Inspect runtime source: verify that after initialization, graph capture for new sequence lengths is dispatched onto a background thread (threading.Thread or concurrent.futures executor) rather than executed synchronously on the main inference thread. Confirm capture stream uses cudaStreamCaptureModeThreadLocal.

sub_tasks.requirements: Communication between static and dynamic domains occurs via device pointers to keep the pipeline fully GPU-resident.

verification.spec: Inspect IPC payload between Context Generator and Graph Generator: verify that tensors are transferred by device pointer / CUDA IPC handle (e.g., tensor.share_memory_() on CUDA tensors, or torch.multiprocessing reductions producing cuda IPC handles) rather than via CPU copy. Assert tensor.device.type == 'cuda' at both ends and data_ptr is preserved across IPC.

sub_tasks.requirements: Explicit CUDA event synchronization is implemented to prevent race conditions while maximizing overlap between streams.

verification.spec: Grep source for torch.cuda.Event usage; verify events are created with enable_timing=False and used via event.record(stream) on one stream and stream.wait_event(event) on another to synchronize between capture stream S_cap and replay stream S_rep.

sub_tasks.requirements: The JIT execution component is implemented for dynamic operations.
PyTorch JIT infrastructure (TorchScript) is used to lower Python-defined dynamic control flow into a statically analyzable intermediate representation.

verification.spec: Grep source for `@torch.jit.script`, `torch.jit.script(...)`, or `torch.jit.trace(...)` applied to dynamic-control-flow functions (preprocessing, sampling, KV-cache update). Verify resulting objects are instances of torch.jit.ScriptFunction or ScriptModule.

sub_tasks.requirements: JIT-compiled regions encapsulate stochastic sampling logic while remaining GPU-resident.

verification.spec: Locate the sampling function; verify it is JIT-compiled (isinstance check on ScriptFunction/ScriptModule) and that, when invoked on a CUDA logits tensor, all intermediate tensors and output remain on the GPU (tensor.device.type=='cuda' throughout). Verify no CPU<->GPU transfers occur (inspect via torch.profiler).

sub_tasks.requirements: JIT-compiled regions encapsulate KV-cache management logic.

verification.spec: Locate the KV-cache update function; verify it is JIT-compiled (ScriptFunction/ScriptModule). Invoke with a sample new key/value tensor; verify cache tensors are updated in place on GPU and that the function handles variable sequence positions (data-dependent index).

sub_tasks.requirements: JIT-compiled regions encapsulate shape adaptation logic for runtime-variable tensor shapes.

verification.spec: Locate the shape-adaptation/normalization function used between dynamic and static domains; verify it is JIT-compiled and accepts inputs with varying sequence-length dimension, producing correctly shaped tensors matching the next CUDA Graph's expected fixed input shape (e.g., via padding/bucketing).

sub_tasks.requirements: Dynamic JIT operations use PyTorch's caching allocator for memory reuse.

verification.spec: Confirm the JIT region does NOT disable the caching allocator (no torch.cuda.caching_allocator_alloc bypass, no PYTORCH_NO_CUDA_MEMORY_CACHING env). Verify allocations during JIT execution go through torch.cuda's caching allocator by checking torch.cuda.memory_allocated()/memory_reserved() before and after, showing reuse rather than monotonic growth.

sub_tasks.requirements: Optimized kernels are integrated within the static graph regions as specified in Section IV-D.
FlashAttention v2 kernels are embedded within static CUDA Graphs for attention computation.

verification.spec: Inspect the attention module of the static path: assert it imports flash_attn (FlashAttention v2) and calls flash_attn_func / flash_attn_with_kvcache, and verify these calls execute inside a CUDA Graph capture region.

sub_tasks.requirements: nvFuser-fused LayerNorm kernels are used within static graphs.

verification.spec: Profile a captured CUDA Graph (via torch.profiler or nsys); verify the kernels executed for LayerNorm are nvFuser-fused (e.g., kernels named `nvfuser_...` or originating from torch._C._jit_pass_fuse / nvFuser code-generated kernels) rather than the default eager `aten::layer_norm` cuDNN kernel.

sub_tasks.requirements: Paged KV-cache kernels from vLLM are integrated within static graphs.

verification.spec: Inspect KV-cache management code: assert it imports vllm paged attention kernels (e.g., vllm._C.ops.paged_attention or vllm.attention.ops) and that the calls occur within CUDA Graph captured regions.

sub_tasks.requirements: Per-decoding-step execution timeline is implemented as four ordered phases.
Step 1: dynamic preprocessing via JIT-compiled shape normalization is executed.

verification.spec: Instrument the runtime decoding step to log the operation sequence; verify that step 1 invokes a JIT-compiled shape-normalization preprocessing path (e.g., torch.jit.script/trace function) on the incoming token context before any CUDA Graph replay or capture is dispatched. Confirm by inspecting that the called callable is a torch.jit.ScriptFunction/ScriptModule and runs on the GPU.

sub_tasks.requirements: Step 2: static graph replay is performed for transformer layers.

verification.spec: Add a hook around the transformer layer execution and assert that, when a matching graph exists, the transformer stack is executed via torch.cuda.CUDAGraph.replay() rather than eager forward. Count kernel launches via Nsight or torch profiler; replay path should yield 1 graph launch instead of many per-layer kernel launches.

sub_tasks.requirements: Step 3: dynamic sampling is performed via JIT to preserve stochasticity.

verification.spec: Verify that the token sampling stage (e.g., temperature/top-k/top-p sampling) is implemented as a JIT-compiled function (torch.jit.ScriptFunction) invoked after graph replay, and that stochasticity is preserved by checking different outputs across two runs with different RNG seeds for the same hidden state.

sub_tasks.requirements: Step 4: asynchronous CUDA Graph capture for future sequence lengths overlaps with the next step's compute.

verification.spec: Instrument the runtime to record CUDA stream IDs and timestamps for capture and replay events. Verify that a capture on the capture stream (Scap) for a not-yet-seen sequence length overlaps in time with replay/compute on the replay stream (Srep) for the current step (their [start,end] intervals intersect on the GPU timeline).
